newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand denies report on possible baht changes.
newsitem.headline: Thailand denies report on possible baht changes.

text.p: Thailand's finance ministry and central bank on Tuesday denied a wire service report which quoted Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan as saying there may have to be a change in the basket of currencies against which the baht is tied.
"Such reports are completely groundless," the finance ministry and the Bank of Thailand said in a joint statement.
The baht came under renewed selling pressure on Tuesday when offshore speculators, especially in Singapore, heavily sold baht for the dollar, dealers said.
The new attack against the baht pushed the baht/dollar sport rate and swap premiums up sharply in the early afternoon trade, dealers said.
The basket of currencies is said to be dominated in weighting by the dollar and is what is used to fix the daily midrate against which the baht is valued against the dollar.

The market has been deluged with rumours about the baht's future recently as it dropped sharply against a surging U.S. dollar. There has also been market speculation that the currency may be devalued but Thai authorities have stressed that would never happen.
